column1: # Guest-callback bridges that call an interface the composed WIT does not declare.
# dispatch in the runtime. An interface the composed WIT never declares cannot be
# imported by any guest, so the call is dead — that shape means a *name* defect
# (a typo, a retired interface), and the only way to say "known, not fixed yet"
# is a line here, which shows up in review.
# Kept apart from `wit-interface-allow.tsv` (wired host interfaces) and
# `wit-op-allow.tsv` (declared-but-unimplemented host ops) because this is the
# third direction: the host calling INTO the guest.
# EMPTY ON PURPOSE: every bridge this list used to excuse has been repaired —
# the glue dispatches it. A line here is the sanctioned way to record a dead
# bridge; there are none left in the tree.
